title: Curve Mirror
description: A roadside convex mirror on an orange pole, standing over an old house at a level crossing in Kyoto. Drag to turn it on its bracket and the glass sweeps everything the photograph never showed: the street behind you, the road below, the sky over your head, and, turned far enough, the house and the crossing you are looking at, seen from where the mirror stands, and the far side of the crossing over your shoulder, its crossbuck and cumulus in a wide convex view against deep cobalt. At one angle it catches the sun.
intent: The Japanese curve mirror (カーブミラー, https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/カーブミラー), the convex road mirror at every blind corner, composited into a real photograph as a physical object, and reflecting correctly. Reality pieces research (factory/reality/techniques.md, idea 7, Curve mirror). The photograph is measured: MoGe-2 metric point map, the true vertical from the poles' vanishing point, the sun from the house's shading. The mirror is a traced sphere cap (800 mm, 1 m radius of curvature: the strongly convex, wide-angle kind) reflecting one panorama centred on it: the photograph itself in front of the lens, its point map marched as a surface from the mirror's position (each ray to its first true crossing, a ray that passes behind a pole or the eave carried on through a background plate with the foreground filled out, so nothing is torn open or speckled; reproject.py), and beyond a vertical plane through the lens at the plate's left edge the far side of the crossing, the plate's own scene turned over that plane (its house, crossbuck and lamps over the viewer's left shoulder, seen from the mirror, with the photographed congestus laid whole as a tower of its own rising behind that crossbuck, sunlit on the sun's side and clear of it), all under the plate's cobalt by elevation; then, behind the lens to the right and below the road's horizon only, a CC0 360 of a Japanese residential street, given the photo's summer sky and the plate's photographed cumulus, and printed to the plate's sun (its contrast, its black, its warm lit white and sky-blue shade), behind it. Four reflected rays per pixel, each from its own point of the face, are marched through that panorama's distances to their first true surface and averaged, so the far side's crossbuck and its pole stand in the glass once, whole and opaque, at their own parallax, and what a board hides from the panorama's centre is read from a far layer with the foreground taken out (the cobalt and the tower), never as a second, ghosted board. Frame (a deep band with a visor over the top), shell, bracket and pole are lit by that panorama and the sun, cast their shadow on the house through the point map, and the glass is an acrylic dome standing proud of the frame, with a Fresnel sheen that climbs to its rim, the zenith's gloss on its upper bulge, the visor reflected at its crown, and dust and a smudge that scatter the sun. The sun in the glass is light, not a paint value: on a float scene its core runs to some twenty times white in its own warm colour, with a warmer skirt drawn close round it, and the Pro-Mist rolls a glow that hot on its brightest channel instead of clipping it to grey, so it blooms warm into cobalt rather than milky. The plate's own enamels are graded down so the mirror is the one warm note against the cobalt (grade.py: where each is; the shader: how much of a pixel is, by a feathered hue window): the crossbuck's yellow to about two thirds of its chroma, turned toward a sun-faded ochre and a third of a stop down, the barrier pole's orange-red to two thirds, the green sign to half, in the plate and in the glass alike. Shot through a Black Pro-Mist (the top 15% of the frame's light, glass and plate alone, spread wide and screened back) and developed through the lab's summer film, its red layer halating a thin warm ring round the clouds, whose sunlit tops (lit in the bake as heaps, from the scene's sun) are carried past the plate's 8 bits so they print as the brightest warm white in the sky. The drag turns it only as far as a real bracket does, 65 degrees either way and 35 down to 15 up, against sprung end-stops that stiffen past 55 and push it back off when let go, so its back is never turned to the lens; its weathered enamel is a rough dielectric (roughness about 0.6, the panorama prefiltered to that width for its sheen, no sun lobe), rolled off under white on the plate's shoulder so the sunlit side stays orange. ?aim=yaw,pitch holds the aim (degrees, held within that range), ?aim=sun holds the sun in the glass, ?aim=hero (-50, 5) holds the far side of the crossing: its crossbuck well inside the rim, the far side's cumulus tower rising behind it over nearly half the glass, and the sun's glint off at the upper rim, in deep cobalt.

sources.author: PJH (@dokae)
sources.note: Ukyo, Kyoto (Ricoh GR II): a low-angle fumikiri crossbuck and lamps over an old tiled house. Resampled to 2464x1632 (photo.webp). Point map, normals and field of view: MoGe-2 ViT-S normal (Microsoft, MIT, https://huggingface.co/Ruicheng/moge-2-vits-normal-onnx) via tools/depth/normals.py; sky matte tools/depth/segment.py sky; its sky graded through that matte to a deep summer cobalt by elevation, deepening toward the zenith, clouds kept pale (sky_grade.py), its own scattered puffs then cleared and a photographed towering cumulus laid in their place (clouds.py, cumulus.py: the summer cumulus congestus below, cut from its own sky by an unmixing matte so its frayed rims and wisps keep their share, mirrored so the scene's sun lights it, its tops graded to the plate's warm sunlit white and its shade toward the skylight's blue), rising from behind the crossing's pole to the frame's edge, its base low behind the roofs, laid over the sky under every wire with the photograph's sharpening halo round the crossbuck and the poles taken out; its enamels graded down (grade.py); the shade side of the crossing's lamp hoods and backplates, and of the crossbuck's bracket, opened with the sky's blue where they face away from the sun, held off the terminator so each keeps a narrow core shadow (shade.py); then the sky composited again as one matte and one grade (matte.py): the whole sky taken to the one cobalt gradient by elevation, the slate band low at the right with it, the cumulus laid again whole from its source (cumulus.py: cut at the source's full 3840 px by a tight unmix, decontaminated, its backlit silver rim held to the body behind it, re-lit by scale to the plate's sun, its broad light a front light of its own dome and its lobes and pockets given back at more than the photograph's contrast, warm white on the sunlit lobes and the skylight's blue in the pockets, taken down to the plate, never up, and given the plate's sharpening and grain), so it is as crisp as the wires across it and its low lobes are one body with it, not decals, and the cold cast taken off the galvanised tower and fittings at the right edge. Baked by tools/depth/bakes/curve-mirror (vp.py vertical, bake.py panorama, distances, SH9, shadow aux; reproject.py rebuilds the panorama toward the crossing and round to the left from the plate alone; farside.py redraws the turned crossing at twice the panorama's resolution from the full-resolution plate, its crossbuck, poles and lamps as planes cut at their depth edges, each with the plate's own antialiased edge, so the far side's board and pole stand in the glass whole and sharp; farheap.py, last, lays the same re-lit cumulus cut again as the far side's tower, so the cloud in the glass is the plate's).

sources.author: AsPJT (Wikimedia Commons)
sources.note: 端陵神社・端陵古墳（南）, March 2025: a 360 at a Japanese residential junction, two lanes, utility poles and wires. The hemisphere behind the lens (the 3840 px rendition, the largest Commons serves to a script): exposed to the photo's sunlit walls, its grey sky (segment.py sky matte at full width, the open sky plus the pockets seen through the canopy) swapped for the photo's graded clear sky by elevation, carried up to the zenith, by unmixing under a feathered, grown matte, so the leaves and the wires stay; the photo's own cumulus carried over the zenith on a cloud plane; then developed to the plate (develop.py): a Lab colour transfer to the photo's sunlit walls per luminance band, the road's highlights rolled off warm half a stop down, its greens desaturated and turned toward the photo's foliage, the pastel in its windows taken out, its tone-mapped crispness let down; then printed to the plate's sun (match.py): its median brought down to sunlit concrete and its lit faces drawn apart from it on a shoulder at the plate's plaster white, white-balanced by light (lit greys to the plaster's warm white, shade to the skylight's blue), its foliage's chroma given back, its edges a little; the plate's photographed cumulus laid over the road behind the lens with the same grade (clouds.massing, in a virtual camera at the plate's focal length), behind the apartment block, the wires and roofs; the circumsolar sky warmed; and a cloud matte (envc.png) so the glass carries those tops past 8 bits as the plate does its own. Last (reproject.py), developed down to the plate's print (its local contrast let down on an edge-aware base, its black lifted to the plate's, its whites held under the plaster's, its colour and edge spread the plate's), its sky rebased on the plate's gradient and crossfaded into it over a wide band, and every cloud a frame cut eroded by its own density toward the cut, so no seam runs straight across the sky.
